title: Federal Appeals Court Rejected Trump Administration Request to Delay Tariff Refund Process
description_medium: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit rejected the Justice Department’s request to pause tariff-refund proceedings for 90 days. The Supreme Court had ruled on Feb. 20 that the administration’s broad tariffs were illegal, allowing importers who paid them to seek refunds. The appeals court sent the next phase to the U.S. Court of International Trade, which would determine how the complex claims should proceed. No refund schedule had yet been set.
description_long: A federal appeals court refused the Trump administration’s request to delay proceedings over refunds for tariffs the Supreme Court had struck down. In a filing, the Justice Department asked the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit to hold off for 90 days; the judges declined and sent the next stage to the U.S. Court of International Trade. The Supreme Court’s Feb. 20 ruling found the tariffs illegal and cleared importers who had paid them to seek refunds, but it did not specify how repayments should work. The government had collected more than $130 billion from the tariffs by mid-December, while a Penn Wharton Budget Model estimate put potential refunds as high as $175 billion. Those figures describe exposure, not money already ordered back to importers. The trade court would need to determine the claims process, and the AP report described no final timetable or individual payment decision. Importers therefore still awaited the trade court’s decision on how the refund process would work.

corrected_wording.reason: Corrects the unsupported claim that the court imposed immediate fiscal consequences; the ruling advanced the refund process but set no schedule.

title: AP Reported 16 Epstein-Related Files Missing From DOJ Webpage
description_medium: The Associated Press reported on Dec. 21, 2025, that 16 files had disappeared from the Justice Department’s public webpage for Epstein-related records. The missing set included an image showing Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell. The Justice Department later restored that photograph after New York prosecutors reviewed it and said no victim appeared in it.
description_long: On Dec. 21, 2025, the Associated Press reported that 16 files had disappeared from the Justice Department webpage hosting Jeffrey Epstein-related records. The group included a photograph of Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell. One day earlier, DOJ had begun publishing a large tranche of Epstein records under a congressional transparency law. The Guardian reported that the photo was flagged by federal prosecutors in New York for review and that Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said removals followed requests from victim-advocacy groups. The Justice Department later restored the photograph after reviewing it and saying no victim appeared in the image; Blanche said the action had nothing to do with Trump. The Guardian also reported that survivors and advocates had raised concerns about identities and images appearing without adequate redaction. The initial AP report counted 16 files removed from the webpage, while the later official explanation described the review and restoration of this photograph. The department said materials would continue to be reviewed and redacted as it received further information.

corrected_wording.original_title: Trump-Era Epstein Portal Missing Files Extended the Credibility Damage Horizon
corrected_wording.reason: Replaces claims of an established integrity breach and extended credibility damage with the reported disappearance and later attributed restoration of one image.

source_access_notes: The AP page did not expose article text in this check; the same-day Guardian report covered the removal and restoration, and Reuters reported the department’s review rationale.
rationale: Replaces claims of an established integrity breach and extended credibility damage with the reported disappearance and later attributed restoration of one image.
revision_reason: Targeted accuracy and reader-copy correction: distinguishes the missing-file count from the restoration of the single photograph and removes process commentary.
